Reading the plots and reporting in a paper

Source: vignettes/reporting.Rmd
reporting.Rmd

The check belongs in the design section of a matched study, next to the balance table, and it is done before any outcome is looked at. This vignette shows how to read the plots and how to build the Methods and Results text from the result, so that every number and setting comes from the run.

library(propsens)
data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
matched <- MatchIt::matchit(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, distance = "glm", link = "linear.logit", replace = TRUE
)
# The faster model set and small settings so the vignette builds quickly; use the defaults
# (logistic regression, BART and the GRF probability forest) in a real analysis.
sensitivity <- propensity_sensitivity(
  matched, algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"),
  seeds = 1:2, n_trees = 100, bootstrap_samples = 5
)

Reading the three plots

Patients plot (plot(x, type = "patients")). Each point is a treated patient: right = the kept models place this patient differently among all patients; up = the kept models give this patient different kinds of untreated partners. The plot describes how the disagreement is spread over the treated patients; it is a description, and individual points should not be read as flags for individual patients. Points near the bottom left mean that these models rank the patient similarly and choose similar partners. Colour shows whether the patient’s logistic score is outside the range of the untreated patients’ scores.

Models plot (plot(x, type = "models")). Each row is a model, each panel a balance statistic, each axis starting at 0. If the points of a panel line up, the balance you report does not depend on the model; if they spread out, it does: say so, and show this plot. Filled points are kept by the quality gate, hollow points are not; your own model has its own colour and is judged on balance only. The extended-terms panel is usually driven by sparse squares and interactions; report the main-terms panel.

Recurrence plot (plot(x, type = "recurrence")). The per-patient pair recurrence behind pair instability (1 minus its mean over treated patients across the kept models; exploratory). Values near the floor (1 / number of kept models) are expected when untreated patients are dense, even when the models agree; report pair instability next to rank disagreement, never alone.

What to write in Methods and Results

methods_text() builds both paragraphs from the result: the model set, the gate and how many models it kept (by algorithm), the matching settings, the share of treated patients kept, the seed and the main summaries. After a fallback it says that all models were used. Edit the sentences to fit your paper.

text <- methods_text(sensitivity)

Methods:

We described the sensitivity of the matched design to the propensity model with the R package propsens (version 0.1.0). Propensity models from logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting (2 seeds for each tree method; 5 models; 5-fold cross-fitted scores; seed 1) were each used for 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching with replacement. Models were kept if their cross-fitted log-loss was within 5 % of the best model’s and their largest post-match standardized mean difference on main terms was within 0.10 of the best model’s and at most 0.25; 3 of 5 models were kept (random forest: 2; gradient boosting: 1), and all treated patients were matched. For the kept models we report the mean rank disagreement over treated patients, the bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model, and the range of the largest standardized mean difference on main terms. No outcome data were used. These summaries are descriptive; they have not been validated as predictors of bias.

Results:

Mean rank disagreement over treated patients was 0.029 across the kept models; the bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model was 0.036. As exploratory summaries, pair instability was 0.52 (of a possible 0.67 with 3 models) and the median between/within-algorithm ratio was 4.5. The largest standardized mean difference on main terms ranged from 0.16 to 0.20 across the kept models.

If you reran the check with several values of seed (seed_sensitivity()), add: “The check was repeated with seeds 1, 2 and 3; all results are reported.”

The text states the balance rule in effect and, after a fallback, that all models were used. Call the criteria pre-specified only if you fixed them before running the check.

If you judge the disagreement to be large

No thresholds exist yet, so this is a judgement you state and justify.

  1. Show the models plot (balance by model).
  2. Choose the design by balance, never by the outcome.
  3. Decide before looking at outcomes whether you will report the effect estimate under each kept model, and then report all of them.
  4. Look at the colour in the patients plot: is the disagreement concentrated among treated patients whose logistic score lies outside the range of the untreated patients’ scores (outside the support, an overlap problem)? Describe this for the study as a whole.

What the check does not do

It does not detect unmeasured confounding, it does not fix a design, and it does not tell you which model is right. When logistic regression is correct, the tree models can still disagree with it: the check describes that the choice matters, not which choice is correct. It cannot tell whether a disagreement matters for the effect estimate, and a small value is not evidence that the estimate is unbiased. It covers 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching for the ATT only.
